```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(SegreCP)
```

`SegreCP` implements sequential component updates on the Segre manifold. A
component is changed, its residual contribution is refreshed immediately, and
the next component sees that new residual. Every tangent proposal uses the
exact rank-`(1, ..., 1)` T-HOSVD retraction.

## Two explicit profiles

The manuscript profile fixes component order and RGD step size, runs the
requested number of full sweeps unless an explicit tolerance is supplied, and
uses no RGN ridge.

```{r}
segre_control(profile = "manuscript", max_iter = 20)
```

The practical profile orders components by current weight, enables an
observable loss-change tolerance, uses backtracking for regression RGD, and
records a small RGN ridge.

```{r}
segre_control(profile = "practical", max_iter = 20)
```

## Initializers

CPCA and HOSVD are both first-class initializers. The example below creates an
orthogonal two-component CP tensor.

```{r}
dims <- c(3, 4, 5)
factors <- lapply(dims, function(p) diag(p)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])
truth <- cp_components(c(3, 1.5), factors)
x <- reconstruct_cp(truth)

init_cpca <- cp_initialize(x, rank = 2, method = "cpca", split = 1)
init_hosvd <- cp_initialize(x, rank = 2, method = "hosvd")

cp_relative_error(init_cpca$comps, truth)
cp_relative_error(init_hosvd$comps, truth)
```

A custom initializer can return a component list directly.

```{r}
custom_init <- function(x, rank, supplied) supplied
fit <- segre_decompose(
  x, rank = 2, method = "rgn",
  init = custom_init,
  init_args = list(supplied = truth),
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 2)
)
fit
```

For decomposition, RGN is the unit-step RGD update because the observation
operator is the identity. In regression, RGN instead solves the restricted
tangent normal equation.
